PLACO+ pleiotropy test on a phenotype pair

Source: vignettes/method-placo.Rmd
method-placo.Rmd

Function: run_placo()

Result column: placo

Family: Pairwise pleiotropy composite-null test

Introduction

Pairwise (traits i,ji,j) test of pleiotropy under the composite null that a variant is associated with at most one of the two traits, using the product of per-trait Z-scores as the test statistic (Ray and Chatterjee, 2020). PLACO is applied to the trait pair only and must be run separately for each pair of interest.

Mathematical Framework and Implementation

For variant vv let Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 be the per-trait Z-scores (β̂/sê\hat\beta/\widehat{\mathrm{se}}). PLACO tests the composite null

H0:β1=0orβ2=0, H_0:\; \beta_1 = 0 \;\mathrm{or}\; \beta_2 = 0,

i.e. the union of the three sub-null configurations (0,0)(0,0), (0,≠0)(0,\ne 0), (≠0,0)(\ne 0,0), against the pleiotropic alternative β1≠0\beta_1 \ne 0and β2≠0\beta_2 \ne 0. The statistic is the product

T=Z1Z2. T = Z_1 Z_2 .

Null density of the product. Under the null each ZkZ_k is approximately normal with mean 0, and (Z1,Z2)(Z_1,Z_2) may be correlated (e.g. through shared controls). Writing rr for that correlation, the density of the standardized product x=Z1Z2x = Z_1 Z_2 is the correlated normal-product density

f(x∣r)=1π1−r2exp⁡(rx1−r2)K0(|x|1−r2), f(x \mid r) = \frac{1}{\pi \sqrt{1-r^2}} \, \exp\!\left(\frac{r\,x}{1-r^2}\right) \, K_0\!\left(\frac{|x|}{1-r^2}\right),

where K0K_0 is the modified Bessel function of the second kind of order 0. The implementation evaluates f(⋅∣r)f(\cdot \mid r) on a power-spaced grid that is dense near 0 (node xi=Xmax(i/(N−1))8x_i = X_{\max}\,(i/(N-1))^{8}) and forms the upper- and lower-tail integrals by reverse-cumulative trapezoidal quadrature, giving a two-sided tail function

G(t)=∫|x|≥tf(x∣r)dx. G(t) = \int_{|x| \ge t} f(x \mid r)\, dx .

Variance and correlation estimation. The null moments are estimated off the variants that are not jointly significant. The per-trait null variances s12,s22s_1^2, s_2^2 are the sample variances of Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 over variants not significant in both traits (i.e. excluding p1<τp_1 < \tau and p2<τp_2 < \tau), where τ\tau is p_threshold. The null correlation rr is the Pearson correlation of (Z1,Z2)(Z_1,Z_2) over variants significant in neither trait (p1≥τp_1 \ge \tau and p2≥τp_2 \ge \tau).

Composite p-value. Because the null is composite, the tail of the product alone is anti-conservative when only one trait is non-null. Following the PLACO construction the p-value uses an inclusion-exclusion combination of the two-sided product tail evaluated at the observed t0=|Z1Z2|t_0 = |Z_1 Z_2| rescaled by each per-trait null SD:

p=G(t0s1)+G(t0s2)−G(t0), p = G\!\left(\frac{t_0}{s_1}\right) + G\!\left(\frac{t_0}{s_2}\right) - G\!\left(t_0\right),

clamped to [10−300,1][10^{-300}, 1]. Small pp indicates evidence that the variant is associated with both traits.

What This Method Advances

PLACO+ targets the composite pleiotropy null directly: association with neither trait or with only one trait should not be called pleiotropic.

Assumptions

  • Per-trait Z-scores are (approximately) standard normal under the respective trait null; departures are absorbed into the empirically estimated null variances s12,s22s_1^2, s_2^2.
  • Cross-trait dependence is captured by a single correlation rr estimated from variants null in both traits; estimation is meaningful only if such variants dominate (sparse true pleiotropy).
  • The product null density is the correlated normal-product law, so the bivariate Z is jointly normal with zero mean under each sub-null.
  • Variants are treated as exchangeable for moment estimation (LD and sample-size heterogeneity are not modelled here).

When This Method Is a Good Fit

Good for pairwise pleiotropy under the composite null of association with at most one trait.

The implementation treats variants independently and relies on the trait-correlation estimate derived from the available summary statistics unless an individual method estimates a pairwise null moment internally.

The empirical variance and null-correlation estimates need enough variants in the relevant non-joint and null/null-like sets. Extremely small simulations, dense signal, or non-finite Z-scores can make those moment estimates unstable.

Pairwise methods use i and j to select the two phenotypes. Re-run the method for each phenotype pair that should be tested.

Minimal Usage 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(1)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3, n_participant = 500,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 3,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(3, 3, 3),
  n_variant_null = 30,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_placo(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
head(pleio@results$placo)

Implementation Files

  • R wrapper: R/run_placo.R
  • C++ kernel or dispatcher: src/placo.cpp
  • Shared MPAT inputs, where applicable: R/pleiotest.R and src/test_engine.cpp
